title: A Parish for the Will
premise: Estate lawyer Petra Blackwood is summoned to probate the will of Edith Marlowe, a woman who vanished twelve years ago and was declared dead—yet the will bears a date signed after her disappearance, and tucked inside it is Edith's diary, its entries continuing for years beyond the day the town buried her memory. As Petra follows the diary's coded references through Ashcombe's ledgers, land deeds, and confessions, she uncovers a conspiracy of prominent families who faked Edith's death to seize her inheritance and silence what she witnessed. The trail leads to a living witness hidden in plain sight, but the conspirators are closing in, and Petra must choose between the law that made her career and the justice it cannot deliver. In the end, Petra exposes the truth at a public reading of the will, Edith's true heir is restored, and Petra trades her invisibility for a town that finally sees her.
about_author: Ivo Coldharbour is the pen name of a former rural solicitor who spent a decade handling estates in small English towns before turning to fiction. Their novels explore how paper—wills, deeds, diaries—holds power long after the people who signed them are gone.

chapters.title: The Reading of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She opens the Marlowe estate file expecting routine probate and finds a will dated three years after Edith Marlowe's disappearance, legally impossible and impeccably executed. Her hands shake as she reads the first line aloud to an empty office. Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into dread.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetized Silence
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback woven with present. We learn how she built her career on keeping Ashcombe's secrets filed and unexamined, including her own small complicity the year Edith vanished. A letter from the firm's senior partner warns her to decline the case. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like water damage.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At home she reads the diary bound with the will; entries continue past the disappearance date, written in Edith's unmistakable hand, describing watchers at her window and a hiding place 'beneath the lych-gate.' Petra realizes someone wants this will found. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by fear of being watched herself.

chapters.title: The Family That Buried Her Twice
chapters.summary: Petra interviews the Halloway family, Edith's cousins who inherited everything in absentia. Patriarch Gerald Halloway is smooth, threatening without saying anything actionable; his son Daniel watches Petra too closely. She notices the family portrait has one frame conspicuously empty. Emotional beat: the chill of polite menace.

chapters.title: What the Constable Kept in His Drawer
chapters.summary: Petra visits retired constable Bill Ferrow, who handled the original missing-person file. He admits the search was called off from above and slips her an evidence bag he never logged: Edith's other shoe, found miles from where she was last seen. Emotional beat: an old man's shame becoming Petra's ammunition.

chapters.title: Lych-Gate
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, night scene. Following the diary's clue, she searches the churchyard and finds a weatherproof box beneath the lych-gate containing more pages—and a photograph of five townspeople, faces circled, including Gerald Halloway and, to her horror, her old mentor. Footsteps approach; she hides. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Mourned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: a woman called 'Nan' tending bees on a remote farm, revealed through habit and half-memories to be Edith herself, alive under another identity, waiting to see if anyone would finally come. She writes a new diary entry: 'Someone is reading.' Emotional beat: loneliness rewarded by cautious hope.

chapters.title: Paper Trails and Burning Bridges
chapters.summary: Petra traces the will's witnesses: both dead, both signatures forged by the same hand—a hand she recognizes from her mentor's old files. When she confronts him, he begs her to stop, revealing only that Edith saw something the night of the harvest festival. Emotional beat: betrayal of the person who taught her the law.

chapters.title: Harvest Night
chapters.summary: Edith's POV via diary entries read by Petra. Twelve years ago, Edith witnessed the Halloways' fatal hit-and-run covered up by the men in the photograph; when she threatened to talk, they staged her drowning. She escaped with help from an unnamed ally—the ally whose handwriting forged the will. Emotional beat: grief for a woman erased while still breathing.

chapters.title: A Break-In Filed Under B
chapters.summary: Petra returns to find her office ransacked, the diary gone, and Daniel Halloway waiting with an offer: a partnership, silence, a comfortable life. She refuses; he leaves a veiled threat about her mother's care home bills. Petra realizes they know exactly how to hurt her. Emotional beat: fear weaponized against her integrity.

chapters.title: The Ally With Two Handwritings
chapters.summary: Petra deduces the ally was the parish vicar, Ruth Ellery, who smuggled Edith out and kept the will safe until someone honest enough appeared. Ruth, dying of illness, confesses all and gives Petra the final diary pages plus a key to a safety deposit box. Emotional beat: an exhausted guardian passing the torch.

chapters.title: Deposit Box 44
chapters.summary: Petra opens the box: original coroner's report suppressed, Edith's real death certificate never filed, and letters proving the Halloways funneled her inheritance through shell companies into their farm empire. She photographs everything and mails copies to three addresses as insurance. Emotional beat: quiet triumph before the storm.

chapters.title: They Know About Nan
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. A strange car passes the farm twice; Nan/Edith packs a go-bag she's kept ready for twelve years. She decides that running again means dying slowly, and instead writes one final entry addressed to whoever is hunting her: 'Come and see what you buried.' Emotional beat: defiance replacing flight.

chapters.title: An Arrest Without Charges
chapters.summary: Petra is detained overnight on fabricated fraud allegations; her files seized, her insurance letters intercepted—or so the Halloways believe. In a holding cell she meets a young officer, DC Amara Osei, who quietly returns one photograph and says, 'My mum cleaned for Edith. She never believed the river story.' Emotional beat: isolation broken by unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: The Town That Knew
chapters.summary: Petra and Osei canvass quietly: the butcher who sold Edith supplies off-book, the nurse who treated her once, the ferryman who rowed her across. Half the town knew fragments; none assembled the whole. Now, given permission, they do. Emotional beat: collective guilt transforming into collective courage.

chapters.title: Gerald's Version
chapters.summary: Gerald Halloway POV. Dying himself, he reflects on the night he decided Edith was worth more drowned than heard, and orders his son to finish the job properly this time. He tells himself it was always about protecting the family name. Emotional beat: self-justifying rot laid bare.

chapters.title: The Farm at First Light
chapters.summary: Daniel and two men arrive at the farm at dawn; Edith meets them on the porch, flanked by the ferryman, the nurse, and Osei arriving with lights flashing—Petra had tipped the constabulary through unofficial channels. Daniel backs down; his father's empire begins visibly crumbling. Emotional beat: the hunted turning to face the hunters.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The police can charge the cover-up but the statute has run out on the conspiracy itself; legal justice will be partial. Petra proposes the alternative: a public reading of the true will at the harvest festival, the same event where Edith was silenced, with the whole town as witness. Emotional beat: choosing the court that matters.

chapters.title: The Second Reading
chapters.summary: Climax. Before the assembled town, Petra reads Edith's will and then Edith herself steps forward, alive, and reads her own diary aloud—the hit-and-run, the staged drowning, every name. Gerald collapses; Daniel is arrested trying to flee; the crowd turns as one body. Emotional beat: catharsis, a town exhaling twelve held years.

chapters.title: Probate for the Living
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Legal aftermath: the estate unfrozen, the shell companies unwound, Ruth Ellery's role honored before her death, Osei promoted for breaking ranks. Edith signs a new will—her first truthful one—with Petra as witness. Emotional beat: restoration, bittersweet and earned.

chapters.title: What Petra Files Away
chapters.summary: Petra closes the Marlowe file and confronts her own archive: she drafts a letter confessing her twelve years of convenient blindness and delivers it to the local paper, ending her invisibility by choice. Some clients leave; others, unexpectedly, thank her. Emotional beat: accountability as liberation.

chapters.title: Beneath the Lych-Gate, Empty
chapters.summary: Final chapter, shared POV between Petra and Edith. They meet at the churchyard where the box once hid; Edith plants daffodils where her secret slept. Petra asks why she chose her; Edith answers, 'Because you alphabetized everything except your conscience.' Petra walks home through a town that nods to her now. Emotional beat: peace, and a watchfulness worth keeping.
